title: Correctness re-run: does the subset pass once the two mechanisms are fixed?
spec: The second half of Evan's T-3 ruling (GA-7, form answer q5): fix and re-run, in its CHEAP form, against the SAME unchanged zero-wrong-answers bar. Three changes, then the same batteries on the same instruments. (1) PIN extra_float_digits = 1 per session and treat anything else as a configuration defect - this cures the value-channel truncation entirely, proven by T-3's own data. (2) Convert the UNICODE-DIGIT GAP into a NAMED REFUSAL. It cannot cheaply be made to match Python - Postgres regexes have no equivalent of Python's any-Unicode-digit class - so the generated SQL raises a named error whenever a rejected string contains non-ASCII digits. Under the standing ruling a loud refusal is an allowed outcome where a silent wrong number is not. (3) The CONTAINER comparison rule goes back to EVAN as its own one-line decision: T-3's investigation was explicit that comparing whole containers with no tolerance is as much a defect of the comparison rule as of the compiler, and that is his call, not this ticket's. Then re-run the three subset fuzz batteries, the fixture, the domain gate and the controls, per setting, unchanged. WHAT A PASS BUYS: admission to T-4, the speed run - NOT admission to GIMS. WHAT TO WATCH: T-3 found unpredicted mechanisms twice, so a third layer is possible; and if T-5's sweep finds non-ASCII digits are common, this fix produces frequent visible refusals and Evan should be asked again before it is treated as the answer.
